n: Psalms 9 and 10 were likely once a single poem; together they form a broken acrostic, with sections starting on successive Hebrew letters. David begins with wholehearted thanks for God’s wonders.

f.g: Wonders — God’s great acts of deliverance.

n: He will be glad and sing praise to the Most High.
When his enemies retreat, they stumble and perish before God’s presence.
God has upheld David’s just cause, sitting on his throne as a righteous judge.

f.w: maintained my right and my cause
f.g: Took up my case in court and ruled in my favor.

n: God has rebuked the nations and erased the names of the wicked forever.

f.w: put out their name for ever

n: The enemy’s ruin is permanent; their cities are uprooted and even the memory of them is gone.

f.w: their memorial is perished with them

n: But the Lord reigns forever; he has set up his throne for judgment.

f.w: the LORD shall endure for ever

n: He will judge the world fairly and govern the nations with justice.
The Lord is a stronghold for the oppressed, a safe tower in times of trouble.

f.g: A high fortress, a secure height out of danger’s reach.

n: Those who know God’s name — his character — trust him, for he never abandons those who seek him.

f.w: hast not forsaken them that seek thee

f.g: Know who God is, his nature and reputation.

n: Sing praise to the Lord who lives in Zion; tell the nations what he has done.

f.w: declare among the people his doings

n: God, who avenges bloodshed, remembers the afflicted and never forgets their cry.
David pleads for mercy: see how my enemies afflict me, you who lift me from the gates of death.
…so that he can praise God in the gates of Zion and rejoice in God’s salvation. Death’s gates contrast with Zion’s gates.

f.g: A poetic name for Jerusalem and its people.

n: The nations have fallen into the pit they dug; their feet are caught in the net they hid.

f.w: sunk down in the pit that they made

n: God is known by his justice: the wicked are trapped by their own deeds. “Higgaion” may be a musical direction.

f.g: Possibly a musical term — a meditative interlude or resounding chord.

f.w: snared in the work of his own hands

n: The wicked and the nations that forget God will return to the realm of the dead.

f.g: Hebrew sheol — the grave or world of departed spirits.

n: The needy will not always be forgotten; the hope of the poor will not die.

f.w: the needy shall not alway be forgotten

n: Rise up, Lord! Don’t let mortals triumph; let the nations be judged before you.

f.g: Don’t let mere humans win out against you.

n: Strike them with awe, Lord, so the nations realize they are only human.

f.w: know themselves to be but men
